'''''Gaudium  myrsinoides''''', commonly known as the '''heath tea-tree''' or '''silky tea-tree''',<ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |title=''Leptospermum myrsinoides'' |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Leptospermum~myrsinoides |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden, Sydney |accessdate=30 April 2020}}</ref> is a species of shrub that is [[Endemism|endemic]] to south-eastern continental Australia. It has smooth bark on the younger stems, narrow egg-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, white flowers and fruit that has the remains of the sepals attached but usually falls from the plant soon after the seeds are released.

==Description==
''Gaudium  myrsinoides'' is a shrub that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|1–2.5|m}}. The older stems have stems with thin, firm bark and younger stems smooth bark that is hairy at first and later shed in stringy strips. The leaves are linear to narrow egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base, {{cvt|5–10|mm}} long and {{cvt|1–3|mm}} wide, tapering to a very short [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]. The flowers are usually borne singly, sometimes in pairs on short side shoots, and are white {{cvt|5–10|mm}} wide and white. There are broad reddish brown [[bract]]s at the base of the flower bud but which usually fall off as the flower opens. The [[Hypanthium|floral cup]] is about {{cvt|4|mm}} long on a very short [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] and is usually silky-hairy only on the lower half. The [[sepal]]s are about {{cvt|0.5|mm}} long, the [[petal]]s {{cvt|4–5|mm}} long and the [[stamen]]s less than {{cvt|1|mm}} long. Flowering mainly occurs from October to November and the fruit is a hemispherical [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] {{cvt|4–6|mm}} wide with the remains of the sepals attached, but which fall from the plant soon after the seeds are released.<ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="Telopea">{{cite journal |last1=Thompson |first1=Joy |title=A revision of the genus ''Leptospermum'' (Myrtaceae) |journal=Telopea |date=1989 |volume=3 |issue=3 |page=369|doi=10.7751/telopea19894902 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |last1=Lyne |first1=Andrew |title=''Gaudium myrsinoides'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/02feed26-e4ba-403f-8488-bf48ef6ad8f2 |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Victoria |accessdate=30 April 2020}}</ref><ref name="seeds">{{cite web |title=''Leptospermum myrsinoides'' |url=https://spapps.environment.sa.gov.au/SeedsOfSA/speciesinformation.html?rid=2644 |publisher=South Australian Seed Conservation Centre |accessdate=30 April 2020}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
This species was first formally described in 1847 by German botanist [[Diederich von Schlechtendal]] who gave it the name ''Leptospermum myrsinoides'' in the journal ''Linnaea: ein Journal für die Botanik in ihrem ganzen Umfange, oder Beiträge zur Pflanzenkunde''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Leptospermum myrsinoides''|url= https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/525976|publisher=APNI|accessdate=30 April 2020}}</ref><ref name="Schltdl.">{{cite journal |last1=von Schlechtendal |first1=Diederich |title=Sudaustralische Pflanzen. II. Bestimmung und Beschreibung der von Dr Behr in Sudaustralien gesammelten Pflanzen |journal=Linnaea: Ein Journal für die Botanik in ihrem ganzen Umfange, oder Beiträge zur Pflanzenkunde |date=1847 |volume=20 |page=653 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/10864#page/656/mode/1up |accessdate=30 April 2020}}</ref> In 2023, [[Peter Gordon Wilson]] transferred the species to the genus ''Gaudium'' as ''G. myrsinoides'' in the journal ''[[Taxon (journal)|Taxon]]''.<ref name="POWO" />

==Distribution and habitat==
The heath tea-tree grows in heath and [[Mallee Woodlands and Shrublands|mallee]] from [[Eden, New South Wales|Eden]] on the far south coast of New South Wales to the [[Mount Lofty Ranges]] and [[Kangaroo Island]] and is widespread in Victoria.<ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="Telopea" /><ref name="RBGV" />
